definition: a disease carried by mosquitoes that causes recurring fever and chills
hook: Malaria is named after a theory doctors got completely wrong.
modernAnchor: It still kills hundreds of thousands of people a year, mostly children, mostly in the tropics.
journey: Italians living near Rome's marshes grew sick again and again, and blamed the fetid swamp air.
They called it mala aria, bad air, certain the stench itself carried the fever into their lungs.
The real killer was a parasite riding mosquito bites, not the smell drifting off the water.
Science replaced the theory a century later, but malaria kept the name of a wrong idea.
